SAG-Wiki 

 
 English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Changelog 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Lightweight and easy. Fast indexing. Precise retrieval. 

 
 A lightweight knowledge base for people and agents. Index and search your local files without LLM calls, then ask questions with answers you can trace to the source.
 

 

PDF basic text can become searchable before background OCR and table enhancement finish. Independent basic indexing keeps supported local Office/RTF documents moving, while PDF segments reuse loaded models. See the changelog for release-specific changes and the documentation site for usage. The download link below points to the latest published stable Release.

 Contents

 
 Project ·
 Technology ·
 User Guide ·
 Agent Guide ·
 Linux Guide ·
 Developer Guide ·
 Community 
 

---

 

 SAG-Wiki in one minute

Download the latest desktop release for macOS and Windows

 Install for your agent 

 

The installer size excludes optional document conversion components and recognition models downloaded on demand.

Add a folder to make your documents, notes, and code searchable. Find a passage, ask a question across files, open the source behind an answer, or give your coding agent access to the same knowledge base.

- Light: no separate database to install; optional recognition components download separately.
- Fast: index a million characters in approximately 200 ms , with no LLM calls for indexing or retrieval.
- Precise: our original SAG2 retrieval technology outperforms RAG, GraphRAG, and other approaches.

The indexing figure above concerns text indexing, excluding document conversion, OCR and table recognition; it is not a whole-PDF completion-time estimate.

Read and edit Markdown, preview HTML, explore related documents, or search from the terminal. PDF, Office, and EPUB documents convert out of the box; image recognition and audio/video transcription are optional components.

For image-heavy DOCX/PPTX files where only text is needed, enable Office text only in Settings → File settings (off by default). Images and embedded objects are skipped before loading; text inside images is not recognized. See the folder guide.

 How it compares

 Capability SAG-Wiki LLM Wiki Typical vector RAG 
 --- --- --- --- 
 Getting started Add a local folder Have an agent read sources and maintain wiki pages Import documents, split them, and build a vector index 
 Preparing knowledge No LLM calls or embeddings An LLM writes and updates summaries and links An embedding model encodes document chunks 
 Knowledge you search Original documents, with passage locations Generated, interlinked wiki pages Indexed document chunks 
 File changes Watch local files and update the index Have the agent revise affected pages Update affected chunks and embeddings 
 Finding information SAG2 evidence retrieval across files Navigate and query the maintained wiki Retrieve by vector similarity, optionally with reranking 
 Everyday use Desktop search, cited Q&A, document editing, and relationship exploration Agent workflows and a Markdown editor Depends on the application 
 Agent access CLI and a ready-to-install Skill Instructions for maintaining and reading the wiki Application-specific tools or APIs 

The comparison uses Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern and the standard vector RAG workflow. Features vary by implementation.

---

 

 Technology

SAG-Wiki runs on SAG2, our original retrieval method . It builds a local index without embeddings or LLM calls, then uses Jev evidence scoring and query-time expansion to find supporting passages across documents. LLMs are used when you choose to generate an answer.

 

 
 
 

 SAG-Wiki is represented by its underlying SAG2 benchmark results. Recall@10 measures evidence recall in the first ten results. SAG2 uses 1,000 questions per benchmark; MuSiQue was used for method development. SAG and BM25 are reference values from the original SAG paper. Difficulty labels are presentation categories; relative gains use the displayed scores. 

 Read the SAG2 paper · For the method, benchmark results, and reproduction code, see SAG-Benchmark .

---

 

 User Guide

 Feature What you need 
 --- --- 
 File indexing and quick search Add a folder; no API key needed 
 SAG2 semantic retrieval Configure a decision model; supply an API key when required 
 Cited Q&A Configure an answer model and API key; SAG2 retrieval also requires a decision model 

SAG-Wiki itself is free and open source. External service charges depend on your chosen provider. Original files stay on your machine; in-depth retrieval and Q&A send the required questions, document passages, or context to the services you configure.

 1. Download, then add a folder or import data

Download the macOS DMG from the latest release link above, open it, and drag SAG Wiki into Applications. The macOS app, bundled CLI, and DMG are Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple.

Install and open SAG-Wiki, switch the sidebar to Folders , then click + beside folder management to add the folder you want to search. Your files stay in their original locations.

 
 
 

 Connect data sources

In the desktop app, open Settings → Data sources to import chats and notes or connect an online platform.

- Chats and notes can be imported from Claude Code, Codex, Evernote, Google Keep, and Apple Notes (macOS).
- Online sources include Notion, Feishu, Lark, Yuque, GitHub, GitLab, DingTalk Docs, Tencent ima, and RSS / Atom. Import on demand or on a schedule.
- Apify runs Actors on demand and imports website content or structured results as Markdown.

See the connection and sync guide for setup steps.

 2. Search your files

Use Search as soon as basic text is indexed. For mixed or scanned PDFs, OCR and table enhancement continue in the background; file-list states show whether basic text is searchable, enhancement is pending/running, or enhancement failed.
